title: Tanaka-san dresses up
setting: A hot weekday morning at the office. Mai tells Yuki that their manager, Tanaka-san, has come in unusually dressed up, and the two of them try to work out why, until he walks over.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: nee, yuki. kesa no tanaka-san, mita?
lines.ja: ねえ、ユキ。今朝の田中さん、見た？
lines.kana: ねえ、ゆき。けさのたなかさん、みた？
lines.english: Hey, Yuki. Did you see Tanaka-san this morning?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: ううん、まだ。どうしたの？
lines.kana: ううん、まだ。どうしたの？
lines.english: No, not yet. Why, what's up with him?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: boushi kabutte kita no. hajimete mita yo.
lines.ja: 帽子かぶってきたの。初めて見たよ。
lines.kana: ぼうしかぶってきたの。はじめてみたよ。
lines.english: He came in wearing a hat. I've never seen that before.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, tanaka-san tte boushi kaburu n da.
lines.ja: え、田中さんって帽子かぶるんだ。
lines.kana: え、たなかさんってぼうしかぶるんだ。
lines.english: Huh, I didn't know Tanaka-san wore hats.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sore ni, nekutai mo shiteru no. itsumo wa shitenai noni.
lines.ja: それに、ネクタイもしてるの。いつもはしてないのに。
lines.kana: それに、ねくたいもしてるの。いつもはしてないのに。
lines.english: And he's got a tie on, too. He never wears one usually.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, konna ni atsui noni? nanika aru no kana.
lines.ja: え、こんなに暑いのに？何かあるのかな。
lines.kana: え、こんなにあついのに？なにかあるのかな。
lines.english: What, in this heat? I wonder if something's going on.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ato ne, kousui mo tsuketeta. sugoku ii nioi shita yo.
lines.ja: あとね、香水もつけてた。すごくいい匂いしたよ。
lines.kana: あとね、こうすいもつけてた。すごくいいにおいしたよ。
lines.english: Oh, and he had perfume on, too. He smelled really nice.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tanaka-san ga kousui tsukeru nante! moshikashite, deeto?
lines.ja: 田中さんが香水つけるなんて！もしかして、デート？
lines.kana: たなかさんがこうすいつけるなんて！もしかして、でーと？
lines.english: Tanaka-san wearing perfume! Don't tell me he's got a date?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.ja: でも田中さん、結婚してるよ。
lines.kana: でもたなかさん、けっこんしてるよ。

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, sou datta. demo yubiwa shiteru no, mita koto nai kamo.
lines.ja: あ、そうだった。でも指輪してるの、見たことないかも。
lines.kana: あ、そうだった。でもゆびわしてるの、みたことないかも。
lines.english: Oh, right. But I don't think I've ever seen him wear a ring.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sore ga ne, kyou wa yubiwa mo shiteru no.
lines.ja: それがね、今日は指輪もしてるの。
lines.kana: それがね、きょうはゆびわもしてるの。
lines.english: Well, that's the thing. Today he's wearing his ring, too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: boushi kabutte, nekutai shite, kousui tsukete, yubiwa made? zettai nanika aru yo!
lines.ja: 帽子かぶって、ネクタイして、香水つけて、指輪まで？絶対何かあるよ！
lines.kana: ぼうしかぶって、ねくたいして、こうすいつけて、ゆびわまで？ぜったいなにかあるよ！
lines.english: A hat, a tie, perfume, and his ring as well? Something's definitely going on!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. nanika atta n desu ka?
lines.ja: おはようございます。何かあったんですか？
lines.kana: おはようございます。なにかあったんですか？

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, ohayou gozaimasu! ano, kyou wa nekutai shiteru n desu ne.
lines.ja: あ、おはようございます！あの、今日はネクタイしてるんですね。
lines.kana: あ、おはようございます！あの、きょうはねくたいしてるんですね。
lines.english: Oh, good morning! Um, I see you're wearing a tie today.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: aa, kore desu ka. jitsu wa kyou de, kekkon shite juu nen na n desu.
lines.ja: ああ、これですか。実は今日で、結婚して十年なんです。
lines.kana: ああ、これですか。じつはきょうで、けっこんしてじゅうねんなんです。
lines.english: Ah, this? Actually, today it's ten years since I got married.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: omedetou gozaimasu! dakara yubiwa mo shite kita n desu ne.
lines.ja: おめでとうございます！だから指輪もしてきたんですね。
lines.kana: おめでとうございます！だからゆびわもしてきたんですね。
lines.english: Congratulations! So that's why you've got your ring on, too.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ee. konban wa tsuma to deeto na node, chotto kakko tsukete mimashita.
lines.ja: ええ。今晩は妻とデートなので、ちょっとかっこつけてみました。
lines.kana: ええ。こんばんはつまとでーとなので、ちょっとかっこつけてみました。
lines.english: Yes. I've got a date with my wife tonight, so I thought I'd try to look sharp.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yappari deeto datta n da! nanka watashi made tenshon agatte kita.
lines.ja: やっぱりデートだったんだ！なんか私までテンション上がってきた。
lines.kana: やっぱりでーとだったんだ！なんかわたしまでてんしょんあがってきた。
lines.english: I knew it was a date! Now I'm all excited too.

questions.english: Why has Tanaka-san come in dressed up today?
questions.ja: 田中さんは今日、何があるんですか？
questions.kana: たなかさんはきょう、なにがあるんですか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san wa kyou, nani ga aru n desu ka?

choices.english: He's going to a friend's wedding after work.
He's meeting an important client at the office today.
It's ten years since he got married, and he has a date with his wife tonight.

questions.explanation: Line 15: kyou de kekkon shite juu nen (today makes ten years since he married), and line 17: konban wa tsuma to deeto (a date with his wife tonight), so he dressed up a little (chotto kakko tsukete mimashita). Yuki's guess of a date was right, just not the way she meant it. A: kekkon is his own marriage, not a friend's wedding. B: nobody mentions a client or a meeting.

questions.english: Mai tells Yuki what Tanaka-san came in wearing this morning. What did she say?
questions.ja: マイさんは、今朝の田中さんについて何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、けさのたなかさんについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, kesa no tanaka-san ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: He came in wearing a hat (kiru, the clothes verb).
He came in with a hat on (kaburu).
He came in with a hat put on (tsukeru).

questions.explanation: Line 3: 'boushi kabutte kita no', and Yuki echoes it in line 4: boushi kaburu n da. Anything pulled over the head (a hat, a cap, a helmet) takes kaburu. A: kiru is for clothes on the body, like a shirt or a coat, so boushi o kiru is the English 'wear' carried over. C: tsukeru is for things put onto the body, like the perfume he also had on (kousui tsuketeta), not for a hat.

questions.english: Yuki says she's never seen Tanaka-san wear a ring. What does Mai tell her?
questions.ja: マイさんは、田中さんの指輪について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、たなかさんのゆびわについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, tanaka-san no yubiwa ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Today he's wearing his ring, too.
He's bought a ring to give his wife tonight.
He's left his ring at home again today.

questions.explanation: Line 11: 'sore ga ne, kyou wa yubiwa mo shiteru no': today he has his ring on as well as the hat, tie and perfume. yubiwa shiteru means the ring is on his finger; nothing is said about buying one (B) or leaving it at home (C). Mai says it to him in line 16 too: dakara yubiwa mo shite kita n desu ne (so that's why you came in wearing your ring).

questions.english: A few days later Tanaka-san is back in his usual open-necked shirt. He has to meet someone important tomorrow, and he asks you, "ashita, daiji na hito ni au n desu kedo, kore de daijoubu deshou ka?" Suggest, politely, that he wear a tie.
questions.ja: 明日、大事な人に会うんですけど、これで大丈夫でしょうか？
questions.kana: あした、だいじなひとにあうんですけど、これでだいじょうぶでしょうか？
questions.romaji: ashita, daiji na hito ni au n desu kedo, kore de daijoubu deshou ka?
questions.answer: Suggest a tie with nekutai o suru, politely since he's your manager: nekutai o shite itta hou ga ii to omoimasu, or nekutai shite kitara dou desu ka? A tie takes suru, never kiru.

modelAnswers.romaji: ichiou, nekutai o shite itta hou ga ii to omoimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: 一応、ネクタイをして行ったほうがいいと思います。
modelAnswers.english: I think you'd better wear a tie, just in case.

modelAnswers.romaji: ashita mo nekutai shite kitara dou desu ka?
modelAnswers.ja: 明日もネクタイしてきたらどうですか？
modelAnswers.english: Why not wear a tie again tomorrow?

questions.explanation: A tie, like a ring or a watch, takes suru: nekutai shite iku is 'go wearing a tie', nekutai shite kuru 'come in wearing one'. In the scene: nekutai mo shiteru no (line 5) and kyou wa nekutai shiteru n desu ne (line 14). nekutai o kiru is the English 'wear' carried over; kiru is only for clothes on the body.

questions.english: You've just got to the office. Mai leans over and says, "are, nanka ii nioi suru ne." Tell her you've got perfume on.
questions.ja: あれ、なんかいい匂いするね。
questions.kana: あれ、なんかいいにおいするね。
questions.romaji: are, nanka ii nioi suru ne.
questions.answer: Say you're wearing perfume with kousui o tsukeru: kousui tsuketeru (it's on) or kousui tsukete kita (I put some on before I came). Not kousui o kiru.

modelAnswers.ja: あ、香水つけてるからかも。

modelAnswers.romaji: kyou wa chotto kousui tsukete kita n da.
modelAnswers.ja: 今日はちょっと香水つけてきたんだ。
modelAnswers.english: I put on a bit of perfume today.

questions.explanation: Perfume takes tsukeru, the verb for anything put onto the body, and tsuketeru means it's on, not that you're putting it on now. In the scene: kousui mo tsuketeta (line 7) and kousui tsukeru nante (line 8). kiru is only for clothes.
